item.title: PicoPCMCIA – a PCMCIA development board for retro-computing enthusiasts
item.description:
📝 While ISA users have enjoyed projects like PicoGUS and PicoMEM, PCMCIA users have long been limited to scarce legacy cards with narrow functionality — this board aims to change that. On devices with very limited power budgets, simultaneous use of networking and audio may require external power. Sound Blaster Emulation Sound Blaster emulation on PCMCIA is particularly challenging, as most PCMCIA sockets and cards lack native DMA support.
🔗 Read more: https://www.yyzkevin.com/picopcmcia/

item.title: Show HN: yolo-cage – AI coding agents that can't exfiltrate secrets
item.description:
📝 And that would be yolo-cage. com/borenstein/yolo-cage/releases/latest/download/yolo-cage -o yolo-cage chmod +x yolo-cage && sudo mv yolo-cage /usr/local/bin/ yolo-cage build --interactive --up Then create a sandbox and start coding: yolo-cage create feature-branch yolo-cage attach feature-branch # Claude in tmux, YOLO mode Prerequisites: Vagrant with libvirt (Linux) or QEMU (macOS, experimental), 8GB RAM, 4 CPUs, GitHub PAT (repo scope), Claude account. CLI Command Description create <branch> Create sandbox attach <branch> Attach (Claude in tmux) shell <branch> Attach (bash) list List sandboxes delete <branch> Delete sandbox port-forward <branch> <port> Forward port from sandbox up / down Start/stop VM upgrade [--rebuild] Upgrade to latest version version Show version Port forwarding Access web apps running inside a sandbox: yolo-cage port-forward feature-x 8080 # localhost:8080 → pod:8080 yolo-cage port-forward feature-x 9000:3000 # localhost:9000 → pod:3000 yolo-cage port-forward feature-x 8080 --bind 0.
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/borenstein/yolo-cage

item.title: Tell HN: Amazon has deactivated my seller account. No idea how to move forward
item.description:
📝 My listings are very clear that this is FOR a Samsung device, and not an actual Samsung device. To reinstate my account, they asked me to submit an authorization letter from the manufacturer or brand owner authorizing me to sell their products. The funny part is that on most of the products I have listed, I am losing money, just because of the FBA costs and the advertising costs.
🔗 Read more: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46709409
